newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy, burying hatchet, welcomes Annan as UN chief.
newsitem.headline: Italy, burying hatchet, welcomes Annan as UN chief.

text.p: Italy, which once came to diplomatic blows with Kofi Annan when he was head of U.N. peacekeeping operations, on Wednesday warmly welcomed his appointment as new Secretary-General and said it trusted he would introduce reform.

"Your long experience, your professional skills and the determination which you have constantly shown...confirm that you will carry out in the best fashion the political leadership and renewal...which the international community expects of the U.N.," President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro said in a message.

Annan infuriated Italy in 1993 when he forced the removal of Italy's commander of troops during a peacekeeping mission in Somalia. Rome said it was "outraged" at Annan's behaviour and plunged into a bitter row with the U.N. over the entire mission.
Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini, in a separate message of congratulations, praised Annan's "very valid contributions" in other roles at the United Nations.
Annan, a 58-year-old U.N. career official from Ghana, on Tuesday called for the world body to become leaner and more effective, as he was sworn in until 2001.
He takes over on January 1 from Boutros Boutros-Ghali of Egypt, whom the United States vetoed for a second term saying he had not done enough to carry out reforms.
Italy has been a leading advocate of reform of the U.N.'s Security Council, which has five permanent members with veto powers and a further 10 members which serve two-year terms.

Italy's stint as a non-permanent member expires this year and it would like to set up a third tier of 20 "semi-permanent" members, 10 of which would sit on the Council at any time, bringing its number to 25. Italy wants to join this tier.

Scalfaro, in his message of congratulations, said the U.N. needed to achieve "greater democracy, fairer geographical representation, efficiency, transparency" and said all countries should be involved in decision-making, regardless of their size.
